grade: 客室乗務員の英語面接

entry.hint: ノックして入室。Good morning. とあいさつしよう

entry.t: Good morning. Please have a seat.

entry.hint: Thank you. と言ってから座ろう

exit.t: That's all for today. Thank you for coming.

exit.hint: お礼を言って退室(Thank you very much for your time.)

varies: 面接の質問は毎回変わります。
origNote: 客室乗務員の英語面接には共通の公式試験はありません。航空会社の面接でよくある流れをもとにした、Babel Flightのオリジナルです。
markNote: 採点は自分でつける目安です。
voiceNote: 面接官の英語はこの端末の音声で読み上げます。面接官は毎回変わります。
sumNote: 会社によって形式は違います。70%をこえたら、英語面接の準備はかなりできています。
flow: 入室 → あいさつ → 着席
面接の質問(自己紹介・志望動機・経験)
機内アナウンスの音読(黙読20秒のあと)
乗客とのロールプレイ

open.t: {hello}My name is {ex}. Thank you for coming today.

close.t: That's all for today. Thank you for coming.

model: Good morning.
Thank you.
Thank you very much for your time.

card.title: Welcome on board
card.passage: Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Welcome aboard Skyline flight two four seven to Fukuoka. Our flight time will be one hour and forty minutes. Please make sure your seat belt is fastened and your seat back is in the upright position. Thank you.

steps.t: Thank you. Now, I'd like you to read an in-flight announcement. Please read it silently first.
All right. Please read it aloud, as if you were on board.
Thank you. Finally, let's do a short role-play. I'm a passenger, and you are a member of the cabin crew. The seat belt sign is on, and you come to my seat.
Excuse me, I ordered a vegetarian meal, but I got chicken.

steps.cue: 謝って、確認すると伝える

steps.t: I really can't eat meat.

steps.cue: 特別食がない場合の代わりを提案する

steps.t: I guess that's OK. I'm quite hungry.

steps.cue: すぐ用意すると伝え、ほかに必要なものを聞く

steps.t: Some water, please.

steps.cue: お礼と、改めてのおわび

points: flight two four seven を数字1つずつ
ゆっくり、笑顔の声で
ladies and gentlemen / fastened の発音

rp1.q: Excuse me, I ordered a vegetarian meal, but I got chicken.
rp1.ja: 謝って、確認すると伝える
model: I'm very sorry about that. Let me check the special meal list for you right away.
points: まず謝罪・共感(I'm sorry to hear that.)
できることを具体的に提案

rp2.ja: 特別食がない場合の代わりを提案する
model: I understand. I'm afraid we don't have another vegetarian meal, but I can offer you some bread, salad and fruit from our other meals.
points: まず謝罪・共感(I'm sorry to hear that.)
できることを具体的に提案

rp3.q: I guess that's OK. I'm quite hungry.
rp3.ja: すぐ用意すると伝え、ほかに必要なものを聞く
model: I'll bring them to you straight away. Would you like something to drink as well?
points: まず謝罪・共感(I'm sorry to hear that.)
できることを具体的に提案

rp4.ja: お礼と、改めてのおわび
model: Of course. Here you are. Again, I apologise for the mistake, and thank you for your patience.
points: まず謝罪・共感(I'm sorry to hear that.)
できることを具体的に提案

card.title: Turbulence
card.passage: Ladies and gentlemen, the captain has turned on the seat belt sign. We are expecting some turbulence. Please return to your seats and fasten your seat belts. The lavatories should not be used at this time. Thank you for your cooperation.

steps.t: Thank you. Now, I'd like you to read an in-flight announcement. Please read it silently first.
All right. Please read it aloud, as if you were on board.
Thank you. Finally, let's do a short role-play. I'm a passenger, and you are a member of the cabin crew. During the flight, you see me looking pale.
Excuse me... I'm feeling sick. I think it's the turbulence.

steps.cue: 共感し、体調をたずねる

steps.t: I feel like I'm going to be sick.

steps.cue: エチケット袋と水を渡す

steps.t: Is the shaking going to stop soon?

steps.cue: 安心させる情報を伝える

steps.t: Thank you. You're very kind.

steps.cue: また様子を見に来ると伝える

points: 落ち着いた、はっきりした声
turbulence / cooperation の発音
文の切れ目で少し間を

rp1.q: Excuse me... I'm feeling sick. I think it's the turbulence.
rp1.ja: 共感し、体調をたずねる
model: I'm sorry you're not feeling well. Can you tell me how you're feeling? Are you dizzy, or do you feel like you might be sick?
points: まず謝罪・共感(I'm sorry to hear that.)
できることを具体的に提案

rp2.q: I feel like I'm going to be sick.
rp2.ja: エチケット袋と水を渡す
model: Here is a sick bag, just in case, and I'll bring you a glass of water. Try to take slow, deep breaths.
points: まず謝罪・共感(I'm sorry to hear that.)
できることを具体的に提案

rp3.q: Is the shaking going to stop soon?
rp3.ja: 安心させる情報を伝える
model: The captain expects it to be smoother in about fifteen minutes. The aircraft is designed to handle turbulence safely.
points: まず謝罪・共感(I'm sorry to hear that.)
できることを具体的に提案

rp4.ja: また様子を見に来ると伝える
model: You're welcome. Please press the call button if you need anything. I'll come back to check on you shortly.
points: まず謝罪・共感(I'm sorry to hear that.)
できることを具体的に提案

card.title: Before landing
card.passage: Ladies and gentlemen, we will be landing at Haneda Airport in about twenty minutes. The local time is three fifteen p.m., and the temperature is eighteen degrees Celsius. Please return your seat to the upright position and make sure your seat belt is fastened. Thank you.

steps.t: Thank you. Now, I'd like you to read an in-flight announcement. Please read it silently first.
All right. Please read it aloud, as if you were on board.
Thank you. Finally, let's do a short role-play. I'm a passenger, and you are a member of the cabin crew. Just before landing, you come to my seat.
Excuse me, my connecting flight leaves in forty minutes. Will I make it?

steps.cue: 不安を受けとめ、便名をたずねる

steps.t: It's flight five one two to Sapporo.

steps.cue: 地上係員に伝えると約束する

steps.t: Can I move to the front so I can get off quickly?

steps.cue: 着陸前は席を移動できないと説明し、代わりの案

steps.t: Thank you so much.

steps.cue: 安心させる言葉

points: 時刻と気温をはっきり
Celsius / position の発音
最後の Thank you. まで笑顔で

rp1.q: Excuse me, my connecting flight leaves in forty minutes. Will I make it?
rp1.ja: 不安を受けとめ、便名をたずねる
model: I understand that you're worried. Could you tell me your connecting flight number, please?
points: まず謝罪・共感(I'm sorry to hear that.)
できることを具体的に提案

rp2.q: It's flight five one two to Sapporo.
rp2.ja: 地上係員に伝えると約束する
model: Thank you. I'll ask the captain to inform our ground staff, so they can help you when we arrive.
points: まず謝罪・共感(I'm sorry to hear that.)
できることを具体的に提案

rp3.q: Can I move to the front so I can get off quickly?
rp3.ja: 着陸前は席を移動できないと説明し、代わりの案
model: I'm afraid you can't change seats now because we're about to land. But I'll ask the other passengers if you can get off first.
points: まず謝罪・共感(I'm sorry to hear that.)
できることを具体的に提案

model: You're welcome. A member of our ground staff will meet you at the gate. Have a good flight to Sapporo.
points: まず謝罪・共感(I'm sorry to hear that.)
できることを具体的に提案

card.title: Departure delay
card.passage: Ladies and gentlemen, this is your cabin crew speaking. We are sorry to inform you that our departure will be delayed by about thirty minutes because of heavy traffic at the airport. We will keep you updated. Thank you for your patience.

steps.t: Thank you. Now, I'd like you to read an in-flight announcement. Please read it silently first.
All right. Please read it aloud, as if you were on board.
Thank you. Finally, let's do a short role-play. I'm a passenger, and you are a member of the cabin crew. Before departure, you come to my seat with your child.
Excuse me, my son and I were given seats in different rows. Can we sit together?

steps.cue: 謝って、席を確認すると伝える

steps.t: He's only six, so I really don't want him to sit alone.

steps.cue: 共感し、隣の乗客に頼んでみると伝える

steps.t: Thank you. And what if they say no?

steps.cue: ほかの案を伝える(空席を探す)

steps.t: That's very kind of you.

steps.cue: お礼と、もう少し待ってもらうよう伝える

points: おわびの気持ちが伝わる声で
delayed / patience の発音
thirty minutes をはっきり

rp1.q: Excuse me, my son and I were given seats in different rows. Can we sit together?
rp1.ja: 謝って、席を確認すると伝える
model: I'm very sorry about that. Let me check the seating for you right away.
points: まず謝罪・共感(I'm sorry to hear that.)
できることを具体的に提案

rp2.q: He's only six, so I really don't want him to sit alone.
rp2.ja: 共感し、隣の乗客に頼んでみると伝える
model: Of course, I completely understand. I'll ask the passenger next to you if they would be happy to swap seats.
points: まず謝罪・共感(I'm sorry to hear that.)
できることを具体的に提案

rp3.q: Thank you. And what if they say no?
rp3.ja: ほかの案を伝える(空席を探す)
model: If that's not possible, I'll look for two empty seats together. The flight isn't completely full today, so I'm sure we can find a solution.
points: まず謝罪・共感(I'm sorry to hear that.)
できることを具体的に提案

rp4.ja: お礼と、もう少し待ってもらうよう伝える
model: You're welcome. Please wait here for a moment. I'll be right back.
points: まず謝罪・共感(I'm sorry to hear that.)
できることを具体的に提案

card.title: After landing
card.passage: Ladies and gentlemen, welcome to Singapore. Please remain seated with your seat belt fastened until the captain has turned off the seat belt sign. Please be careful when opening the overhead bins, as items may have moved during the flight. Thank you for flying with Skyline.

steps.t: Thank you. Now, I'd like you to read an in-flight announcement. Please read it silently first.
All right. Please read it aloud, as if you were on board.
Thank you. Finally, let's do a short role-play. I'm a passenger, and you are a member of the cabin crew. After landing, an elderly passenger calls me.
Excuse me, I can't reach my bag in the overhead bin. It's very heavy.

steps.cue: 手伝うと申し出る

steps.t: Thank you. Also, my knees are not very good. Is there a wheelchair?

steps.cue: 車いすを手配すると伝える

steps.t: How long will it take?

steps.cue: 待ち時間の目安と、先に降りる人を待つよう伝える

steps.t: You're very helpful. Thank you.

steps.cue: 最後のあいさつ

points: Singapore / overhead bins の発音
until の前で少し区切る
最後の Thank you for flying … は明るく

rp1.q: Excuse me, I can't reach my bag in the overhead bin. It's very heavy.
model: Of course. Please stay in your seat, and I'll take it down for you once the seat belt sign is off.
points: まず謝罪・共感(I'm sorry to hear that.)
できることを具体的に提案

rp2.q: Thank you. Also, my knees are not very good. Is there a wheelchair?
rp2.ja: 車いすを手配すると伝える
model: I'm sorry to hear that. I'll ask our ground staff to bring a wheelchair to the aircraft door for you.
points: まず謝罪・共感(I'm sorry to hear that.)
できることを具体的に提案

rp3.ja: 待ち時間の目安と、先に降りる人を待つよう伝える
model: It usually takes about ten minutes. Please wait until the other passengers have left, and I'll come and get you.
points: まず謝罪・共感(I'm sorry to hear that.)
できることを具体的に提案

model: It's my pleasure. Thank you for flying with us, and I hope you enjoy your stay in Singapore.
points: まず謝罪・共感(I'm sorry to hear that.)
できることを具体的に提案

crew_q.ja: 自己紹介をしてください。
model: Good morning. My name is Yuki Sato. I'm a university student majoring in international communication. I enjoy meeting people from different cultures, and I have worked part-time at a hotel for two years.
points: 1分以内
名前 → 学校・仕事 → 強み

crew_q.q: Why do you want to become a cabin attendant?
crew_q.ja: なぜ客室乗務員になりたいのですか。
model: Because I want a job where I can make people's journeys safe and comfortable. When I flew abroad as a child, a cabin attendant helped me when I was nervous, and I still remember her kindness.
points: きっかけの体験
安全と快適さの両方

crew_q.q: Why did you choose our airline?
crew_q.ja: なぜ当社を選んだのですか。
model: I was impressed by your service when I flew with you last year, especially the way the crew paid attention to each passenger. I would like to be part of that team.
points: 具体的な体験
その会社らしさ

crew_q.q: Tell me about a time you dealt with a difficult customer.
crew_q.ja: 難しいお客さまに対応した経験を話してください。
model: At my part-time job at a hotel, a guest was angry because his room was not ready. I listened carefully, apologised, and offered him a seat in the lounge with a drink. In the end, he thanked me.
points: 状況 → 行動 → 結果(STAR)

crew_q.ja: あなたの強みは何ですか。
model: My strength is staying calm under pressure. In my club activities, I was the captain, and I had to make quick decisions during matches.
points: 強み + 具体例

crew_q.q: How do you work in a team?
crew_q.ja: チームでどのように働きますか。
model: I try to communicate clearly and help others when they are busy. I believe good teamwork is important for safety on board.
points: 安全とのつながり

crew_q.q: How would you stay calm in an emergency on board?
crew_q.ja: 機内の緊急事態でどうやって冷静でいますか。
model: I would remember my training and follow the procedures step by step. Passengers watch the crew, so staying calm and giving clear instructions helps them stay calm too.
points: 訓練・手順
乗客への影響

crew_q.q: What does good customer service mean to you?
crew_q.ja: あなたにとってよいサービスとは何ですか。
model: For me, good service means noticing what passengers need before they ask. For example, offering a blanket to someone who looks cold.
points: 自分の言葉で定義 + 例

crew_q.q: How do you deal with stress?
crew_q.ja: ストレスにどう対処しますか。
model: I try to get enough sleep and go for a run when I can. I also talk with friends, which helps me relax.
points: 具体的な方法

crew_q.q: Tell me about a time you worked with people from different cultures.
crew_q.ja: 異なる文化の人と働いた経験を話してください。
model: At my part-time job at a hotel, I worked with staff from Vietnam and Nepal. I learned to explain things simply and to respect different ways of working.
points: 状況 → 学んだこと

crew_q.q: Where do you see yourself in five years?
crew_q.ja: 5年後、どうなっていたいですか。
model: I hope to be an experienced cabin attendant who can train new members of the crew, and to work on international routes.
points: 成長のイメージ

crew_q.q: What would you do if a passenger refused to fasten their seat belt?
crew_q.ja: 乗客がシートベルトを締めてくれなかったらどうしますか。
model: I would politely explain that it is for their safety and that it is a rule. If they still refused, I would inform the senior cabin crew member.
points: ていねいに理由
上司への報告
